name: US jobless claims
summary: US jobless claims 4-week average 194,750, at its 52-week low; next release due 12 Nov
state: Initial US jobless claims were 189,000 in the week to 31 Oct, keeping the four-week average at 194,750, its 52-week low and far below the 15% Watch line (Department of Labor via FRED). Strong October payrolls data also pointed to a firm labour market (Yahoo Finance, 10 Nov). The next weekly figure is due on 12 Nov.
for_you: Layoffs remain low by historical standards, so most US workers face little immediate pressure on job security.
why: Weekly claims are the earliest hard data on US layoffs; a sustained rise usually comes before the unemployment rate turns.
drivers: Layoffs, hiring freezes, federal job cuts, storms, strikes and seasonal quirks.

rubric.normal: The 4-week average of initial claims is less than 15% above its 52-week low.
